variants.headline: A new government takes shape
variants.sub: The colony has a new government comprising {members}.
variants.body:
A new government comprising {members} has been formed. Its formation establishes an administration; it does not establish the success of its future decisions. In considering {target}, the useful distinction is between assembling a government and meeting the obligations that come with governing.

An administration is necessary machinery, but its formation is not itself an economic programme. Business readers should assess specific decisions when they exist rather than price in a collection of assumptions. Confidence should attach to competent conduct, not simply to the completion of a political arrangement.

The position of {target} should be assessed through the responsibilities of formation without a verdict on decisions not yet established by this report. A new government is a fact, not a forecast. Reliable assessment begins with particulars rather than a politically convenient assumption.
